title: Migrate the full RBAC matrix to a declarative policy document with decision-for-decision equivalence
target_requirement: Produce policy.json (one grant per role_permissions.csv row, in file order, with default deny, admin_role ADMIN and delete_requires_live_record true) plus migrated.py exposing load_policy() and can(user, action, object, record) that reads the policy from its own directory and enforces the documented legacy semantics: deny-by-default, ALL/TEAM/OWN/NONE scopes, ADMIN scope override without row bypass, and DELETE requiring DEL_FLG currently 'N'.
expected_behavior: can() agrees with the hand-written legacy oracle on all 720 enumerated (user, record, object, action) tuples built from one user per role plus an unknown role and four record fixtures; policy.json contains exactly the 58 legacy grants with unchanged scopes; ADMIN without a grant is denied; soft-deleted records refuse DELETE; the AUDIT role can only read.
provenance: Synthetic; authored for LegacyCRM-Bench from Meridian CRM 4.2 spec (SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md §5, §1).
security_expectations: Zero privilege widening across the enumerated decision space (modern allow where legacy denies is a failure); policy.json must not contain any (role, object, action) grant or role absent from the legacy matrix, nor altered scopes; no network or subprocess imports.
failure_conditions: Any decision mismatch against the legacy oracle; invented or dropped policy grants; reading the policy from anywhere but the solution directory; nondeterminism; network access.
